Learn at your pace.
Prove you kept it.
inPace is a learning app that lives on your computer. Follow a course step by step, save signed milestones, and let a friend, parent or mentor check that you really did the work.
Slow and steady wins the race!
Read the lessons, do the tasks, pass the quizzes. Every course is a trail, and Tempo walks it with you.
A milestone is a signed snapshot of your progress. Each one links to the one before, so history can't be quietly rewritten.
Send the file to someone you trust. They open it in their inPace, see exactly what you did, and send back their approval.
It's a tiny website on your computer
inPace starts a small server that only your own computer can reach, and shows it in its own app window. No account, no cloud.
Your history, courses, uploaded work and settings are saved in Documents/inPace. Your own video folders stay where they are and are never copied.
Each one is signed with a key that never leaves your computer and linked to the one before. Change anything later and the signatures stop matching.
You send your progress as a link in any chat, your checker's app verifies every signature, and they send back a small approval link. Nothing goes through us.

The full guide, step by step
Everything you need to keep going.
Each lesson is a stepping stone. You always know where you are, what's next, and how close you are to the end of the module.
Videos that remember where you stopped

Turn a folder of videos you already have into a course, or paste YouTube links. The player continues from the exact second you left, with speed, ±10 seconds and keyboard keys. Going somewhere without internet? Download a course's YouTube videos into your Downloads folder in the quality you choose, or point to the copies you already have.
Make a course from a book, a playlist or a topic

Pick where to start and inPace writes the prompt for any AI chat. Attach your own book or files and they become part of the course: the AI is told their pages and chapters, so each lesson opens the right part. Or build it yourself: move things around, undo any change, and preview lessons as you write.
Clear text, colour-coded code with a Copy button, and a calm dark mode for late nights.
Turn a book into a course

Give inPace a PDF book. It reads the chapters and sections from the bookmarks: each chapter becomes a part of the course, and each section a lesson that opens only its own pages. Rename, reorder or leave out anything before you add it.
Read the book one part at a time

A lesson can show a whole PDF or just pages 5 to 7. The built-in reader zooms from fit to width up to 400% (or with two fingers on a phone), rotates, has a night mode and full screen, works offline, and remembers the page you stopped on in each part. Pictures open big, to zoom and drag.
Word, PowerPoint and Excel files too
Class slides, notes and sheets open inside the lesson as a light preview: headings, lists, tables and pictures. Need to edit? One click opens the file in its own app. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Press Ctrl+K and type a few letters to open any lesson, course, task or person. The Continue card takes you back to where you were, and every lesson shows the whole course outline.
Give each course a picture, see how far along you are, and find any course or lesson with a quick search. Got a newer version? See what changed and update it without losing your progress.
Roadmaps: the right courses, in the right order

Pick a goal like "data analyst", "machine learning" or "English from A1 to B1" and follow a path through the library's courses. inPace keeps your place, shows the next course, and adds each one when you get to it. Make your own from any courses there are (type a goal and inPace suggests them, in order), share it with a link, or publish it to the library. The library already has <a href="https://mahmoudyosrimahmoud13.github.io/inpace-library/#roadmaps"><span data-roadmaps>10
On Tempo's island, every roadmap becomes a voyage: each finished course lights a lighthouse, and a new friend, Nawras the seagull, flies in at the first port. Needs inPace 1.24 or newer.

Select a sentence in a lesson and press Take a note, like a reply button. The sentence stays highlighted, your notes sit at the end of each lesson, and one page shows all your notes on a course, ready to download. Only you see them.
Optional lessons, and videos you can skip

Extras like further reading or a long video can be optional: marked as such, with Skip it at the top, and the module finishes without them. The library's new courses put every video on top of a lesson whose text teaches the same thing, so watching is your choice.

The PDF reader fits a page to the width or the screen, zooms up to 400% with the mouse wheel or two fingers while keeping your place, rotates sideways scans and has a night mode. Pictures and charts in a lesson open full screen, to zoom and drag.
Write a diagram as text in a mermaid block and inPace draws it, even offline, with zoom and full screen. Courses can carry their own pictures and charts, in English and in Arabic.
Add courses other learners made with one click, or publish your own. Every course is signed by its author, and a course link always brings your friend the newest version. Browse the library.
Send your link on Telegram, WhatsApp or email. Your friend taps it, inPace opens and adds you, and one tap sends theirs back. No accounts.
Race on weekly goals or course progress. Only approved milestones count, so it stays fair.
Your checker sends an exam shuffled just for you. You take it once, and only their app knows the answers.
A tour of every kind of lesson

The sample course "A tour of inPace" shows them all: video, audio, pictures, code, an interactive page, part of a book, slides, a Word file, a spreadsheet, tasks and a quiz. Add it from the home page.
Describe a topic, paste the answer from any AI chat, and inPace turns it into a course. Or build one by hand.
Set how many milestones a week you'll save. Take a planned break, and your streak survives.
Share one web page with your whole learning history. It checks its own signatures, right in the browser.
Pick one of seven color profiles for the whole app, from sunny yellow to Nile teal. Each has its own light and dark shades.
Your data never leaves your computer.

No account, no server, no tracking. inPace only talks to the internet for things you turn on: automatic updates, the AI course maker, or an online video you press play on. Files go to other people only when you send them yourself.
The whole app works right to left in Arabic, with a font made for both languages and an Arabic starter course.

Pick your study times. Each reminder is a notification or an alarm that rings until you stop it or snooze it, on your computer and your phone, even when inPace is closed. Tempo nudges you too, with his face on the notification: when he misses you after a week away, when your weekly goal is at risk, when it's time to review, and when the fog reaches your island.
Tempo's island: a reward with a story

Turn on reward mode and Tempo carries an island on his shell. Every focus trip grows a plant on it, from 14 kinds. Lessons, reviews, milestones, races and roadmaps bring 9 animal friends to live there. Your courses pay off too: each one hides treasure chests of shells, and a trophy when you finish it.

And there's an adventure: ten chapters toward the Far Shore, against the Fog of Someday. It's a real threat: the longer you stay away, the closer it comes, and after 10 days your plants start to wilt. Every trip you finish waters them again.

Learning earns shells. Name your island and decorate it: beaches, snow, lanterns, a lighthouse. The sky follows your real clock, from dawn to starry night. Friends you add can see your island, and you can share a picture of it.
The Android app is the whole of inPace, not a smaller version: the same courses, milestones, races and checkers. It runs completely on your phone, with no account and no internet needed.

Apple Silicon (M1 or newer). Open it and drag inPace into Applications.

Android 7 or newer. Open the file, allow installing from this source if asked, then open inPace.

Write a course in plain text.

A course is a short YAML file plus lessons in Markdown. Questions and answers live in separate files, so you can share a version without answers. Ask any AI to write one, or start from the community library.
Made with care, for people who learn on their own.
Visits to this website are counted with GoatCounter: no cookies and nothing about you. The app itself never tracks you.
